lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Oof, I'm finally here! At least the 6 hours went by fast on Delta One! ;)

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: TATA! You're BACK!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We waited for you for a hundred years.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A hundred MILLION years!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, up! Up up up!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm the tallest! Giddyup, Tata!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello, Rose. Please keep your arms and legs inside the uncle at all times.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, LOOK. A sparkling diamond gold dumpling squishy!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's limited edition. There are only two in the whole world. You can squeeze it!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's the shiniest dumpling I've ever seen. And I've seen a LOT of dumplings.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Come on, Tata! Let's go!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata! Deedee made rhubarb crisp for you. It's cooling RIGHT NOW.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I already licked the spoon. Don't tell.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we had better hurry. Before somebody licks the rest.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: My favorite son!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And my girls! Come here, come here.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, look at the door. Deedee measured me two times since you left.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I got one too. Mine's the low one.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom, you must be starving! Sit. The crisp needs ten minutes on the counter.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Where are my reading glasses? I had them one second ago. I need to read the timer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Deedee. They're on your head.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: So they are. Not one word to Boppy.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I brought you a sourdough loaf. Baked it yesterday. It flew here on my lap.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Your bread and my rhubarb crisp. Now THAT is a meal.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: A sliver for me. Just a sliver. Sourdough gives me gas.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom, EVERYTHING gives you gas.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And I eat it anyway. That's love, Tom.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom! Good. I'm not feeling good. It's the stomach.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee! A mud blob just climbed in the window, and it's running off with your crisp!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: A WHAT climbed in my window?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It has EYES! The mud has EYES!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Forty years in this kitchen. I've had ants. I've had a raccoon. I have never had THAT.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's so brown. It's the brownest thing I've ever seen.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That was UNCALLED for!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's running for the pond!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: It took the crisp AND my good tin! Grab your shoes, everybody. We're going after it, and I'm coming with you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: It's headed for Grump Hollow. I've been saying for twenty years that something lives in that pond, and nobody listens to Boppy.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Twenty years ago I'd have caught that thing before it got to the fence.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'd come with you, but my stomach is acting up. If you see the Big One in that pond, bring him back for me.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom. You stay in front of those girls.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Look, rhubarb crumbs on the path. The little thief dropped them as it ran, so we can follow the trail.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. The mud is MOVING.

lines.speaker: Mudling
lines.text: Blub. The pie went that way. You can't have it. Blub.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It talks.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: It talks AND it steals.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Okay, everybody. Tata is in front. I'm in charge of choreography. FIGHT!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There. Good as new. Try not to do that again.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Good job, girls. The crumb trail keeps going north, so that's the way we go.

lines.speaker: Skeeter Swarm
lines.text: Bzzz. Somebody smells like rhubarb. Bzzzzz.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Ew. Ew ew ew. Nobody touch my hair.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I've been bitten ten thousand times in my life. Not one of them ever said a word first.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There. Good as new. Try not to do that again.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Everybody okay? Itchy isn't hurt. Keep walking.

lines.speaker: Pond Grump
lines.text: Grrrumble. You're standing in my puddle. And the small one is LAUGHING at me.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm not laughing. I'm giggling. It's different.

lines.speaker: Pond Grump
lines.text: That's IT. Soggy Slap. For the giggler.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There. Good as new. Try not to do that again.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Hugs for everyone. There. All better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The crumbs lead around the pond, toward Boppy's fishing spot.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy says the Big One lives over there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then nobody goes near the water. Stay close.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A MARBLE! There's a marble with a bug in it!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's a dragonfly. It's inside an orange rock. Its wings are open and it's not moving.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Look at the grass. It's grey. Just this bit, the size of my hand.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It isn't dried out. It's just grey. Like somebody took the green out.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm keeping it. It's stuck.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Let me.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: You're not trying.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I'm trying, Rose. It's a marble and it's winning.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: There's a little round hole in the side. Like somebody took a bite.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And somebody left a burnt light bulb. Now they're littering at my pond too.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The tin. Go, go, go.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Bye, marble. I'm coming back for you.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: THERE! The thief! He still has the tin!

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: GLUB. Is that a pie? For me?

lines.speaker: Big Mudling
lines.text: Blub. I stole it for you, boss.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: The tin fits on my head like a crown. I'm the king of the pond now. GLUB.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's a fish. That fish is bigger than the cab.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy was RIGHT?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nobody tell him.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: That's my GOOD tin, you overgrown handbag!

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: This morning I was a fish. Then there was a big flash. Now I am a BIG fish. With a hat.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, he looks like a turtle wearing a hat.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody touches Deedee’s crisp. Everybody ready?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom, you stand in front of whoever it stares at. Cozy Rosie, make it laugh. Then we try again.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: Glub. Nobody ever made me laugh before. You can have your tin back.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: Glub. Fine. Take your tin. I'm going back in the pond to think about things.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: And this is for the small one. It's my shiniest thing.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It has a bug on it! I'm keeping it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: This one you can keep.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: The old man with the cap. Is he coming tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy? He comes every day.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: Good. Don't tell him I asked.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: My tin! And look. Half the crisp is still in it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The Big One ate the other half. I saw crumbs on its chin.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Then we split this half. Everybody home. Wait until Boppy hears about this.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You found the Big One? I TOLD everybody. Twenty years.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy, the mud TALKED. And the mosquitoes. And a puddle.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The mud talked? Forty years in this town, the mud never said one word to me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We did. And when it laughed, this fell out of its lip.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My LURE! I lost that in 2006. Still shiny. Unlike me.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Keep it, Tom. For luck. The fish clearly didn't want it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He gave me a present. Look.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's real gold, Cozy Rosie. Gold like my teeth. Look.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy has treasure in his mouth!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You put that somewhere safe. Gold is for keeping.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Next time something comes in that window, I'm coming. Stomach or no stomach.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Sit. Everybody sit. Half a crisp is still a crisp.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: This is the best half a crisp I ever had.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, you're staying the WHOLE week, right?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The whole week. And nobody is stealing anything else.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Slow down. Everybody eats too fast. My stomach.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB said he'd be home. Spring Street loft.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...He said he'd be home.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Well, well, well...

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look who flew three thousand miles to see me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I flew three thousand miles to see you... and maybe the starter.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Main event. I'll take it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: My call time got pushed to Thursday. The lead actor lost a shoe. I already found it. So I'm all yours.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Also, something is up. The sky over Griffith Park went purple this morning. Not sunset purple. Weird purple.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: All yours. I like that. We'll go look at the purple sky together, but first I need one quick stop at my house.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: My sourdough starter has been alone for a week.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Olivia dropped her off this morning. Family trip to the desert. No dogs at the hotel.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's been sitting on your porch since eight. I tried to take her to the loft. She refused.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Also, your starter was bubbling out of the jar, so I baked a boule with it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I'm proud. As long as you didn't spin it on your pottery wheel.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Tom tears off the heel and holds it up. "Sit." Nara sits, wiggling all over. "Paw." She gives him her paw. Very, very hard.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: She gets the bread. Tom gets a lick.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sit, paw, treat. She knows the whole routine. So polite!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello, Bready Mercury. Did you miss me? You missed me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. Stir. Look at those bubbles.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You talk to that jar more than you talk to me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The jar gets fifty grams of flour. You get the whole week.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...And you steamed my shirts for the flight. You win. You always win.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'll take it.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara is at the front window, whining. Her tail is down.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Look outside. Is the street... purple?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Washington! Is everything okay?

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Tom. Back in 1979, this whole block...

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He's been saying that for a while, babe.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Such a nice afternoon. It should always be this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me, smog. That was UNCALLED for.

lines.speaker: Smoglet
lines.text: Cough. Nice street. We're going to sit on it for a while. Forever, actually.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Remember movie night? You threw the whole popcorn bowl.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I was startled. Briefly. With dignity.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It was a battle plan. You just didn't know it yet.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Okay. Everybody breathe. Through the nose. Not the smog.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The smog monsters are gone, but Mr. Washington is still in a daze. Look at him.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Nobody needs to go anywhere. Nobody needs to get any older.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Washington would never say that. The smog is doing something to him. Let's go check on Miss Odette and Doña Carmen on the boulevard.

lines.speaker: Miss Odette
lines.text: Stirring. Stirring. The gumbo never has to be done, baby. Isn’t that nice?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's made that gumbo every day for fifty years. It's never once been "never done."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The smog makes people want everything to stay exactly the same forever. That's not a nice afternoon. That's a hostage situation.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: The pupusas are fine. Everything is fine. It's always this afternoon. Why did I ever flip them?

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara sniffs the comal. She sneezes. The smoke smells like the hills.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Nara is right. That's not kitchen smoke. It's the same purple smog, and it's blowing down from the hills.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Look north. It's all coming down off the hills.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It's coming from the Observatory. The pipes on its side are pumping out smog like a smoke machine on a bad set.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then that's where we're going. Nara, stay close.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara presses against Tom’s leg. She's not letting him go anywhere without her.

lines.speaker: Ticket Flurry
lines.text: Street cleaning. Tuesday. Eight to ten. You didn't read the sign. And the smog says we can stay forever.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I take the Metro. You have nothing on me.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Up, everybody. Wardrobe says nobody is cut from this scene.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I contest that ticket, and I'm granting my own appeal. Let's keep going.

lines.speaker: Canyon Coyote
lines.text: Nice hike. You look like you have snacks. And the dog looks like a snack.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara’s hackles go up. She stands right in front of Tom.

lines.speaker: Canyon Coyote
lines.text: Pack Howl. For the fluffy one.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Up, everybody. Wardrobe says nobody is cut from this scene.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Quick wardrobe adjustment, quick heal, and a quick kiss for the road. Ready, babe?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Ready. Kiss accepted. The Observatory is up at the top left. Follow the purple.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The ground is humming. That's never a good sign. I've seen this movie forty-seven times.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: RUMBLE. A man in a long coat plugged my vents.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Now all my grumbling comes out of those pipes as purple smog, and everything it touches gets stuck. And I LIKE stuck.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: When everything is stuck, nothing moves and nothing changes, and nobody ever has to say goodbye.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: That's what the man promised me. Nobody leaves. Not ever.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody says goodbye. Then they come back. That's what planes are for.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Things have to move.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara barks at the hill. Once. Very loudly. Then she checks that Tom saw.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Well, well, well... looks like we're in a bit of a shaky situation.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Cut. Reset. Back to one, everybody.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, heal right after the Aftershock. When it clogs up, hit it with water or sparkle. Or one of our Tombos.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Rumble. You asked how I was doing. Nobody has asked in a million years.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: ...I'll let things move. A little. Two inches a year. That's my best offer.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Rumble. Fine. The pipes are clear. I'm going back under the hill to think about my choices.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look. The sky is blue again. Los Angeles blue. Slightly brown, but blue.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: So a man in a long coat plugged those vents on purpose. He wanted this whole city stuck in one afternoon. I'd like to know why.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Spooky. I love it. Let's go check on Mr. Washington.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: ...smelled like gumbo on a Saturday night. Zydeco from the boulevard. Kids on every porch.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Where was I? Oh. I was done. That was the whole story.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Funny. For a while there I didn't want anything to change. Then I remembered the best parts all came from things changing.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Keep the old windows, though.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Keep the old windows. Smart man.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Doña Carmen says the pupusas came out perfectly crispy. Miss Odette is sending over gumbo. The whole block is cooking.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara leans on both of them at once. Tiny excited puddle. Nobody minds.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Long Island is home, and so is this. I have two homes. Okay. Good.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata! Boppy has been waiting by his window since BREAKFAST. He has his fishing hat on.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He said if you were late he'd catch the fish without you. He catches one every time. It's always THIS big.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we'd better hurry, before it gets any bigger.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: My favorite son!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Back already! Look at you. Did they feed you out there? Never mind. I'll feed you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom. Good. Sit down. No. Don't sit down. We're going fishing.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The Whisker Perch. Whiskers like a cat. I saw it at Cattail Pier in 1994. Nobody believes me.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nobody believes him.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, is the Whisker Perch real?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Real as my heartburn, kiddo.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm bringing a notebook. For science. And for proof.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: And I'm bringing THIS. My pepper jar. Homegrown, pickled in 1989. Older than your mother.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Not one pepper for me either. Peppers give me gas.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Deedee. EVERYTHING gives you gas.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Who told you that.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. At the crisp.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tata is on thin ice.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I have three pies in, so I'm staying put. Do NOT let him eat peppers on an empty stomach.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I never eat peppers on an empty stomach. I eat them on a full stomach. Then it's empty.

lines.speaker: Oolong
lines.text: Boppy! The usual? Ginger, peppermint, and a little honey for the stomach.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The stomach thanks you. The stomach is still complaining. But it thanks you.

lines.speaker: The kettle
lines.text: The kettle whistles, low and long. Oolong leans in to listen.

lines.speaker: Oolong
lines.text: The kettle says a man in a long coat has been buying up gold coins at Penny's shop. He pays double, and he never takes his hat off.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: On Long Island? Nobody here pays double for anything.

lines.speaker: Oolong
lines.text: The kettle also says it'll rain on Tuesday. The kettle is wrong a lot. Enjoy the pier.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Did I ever tell you about 1970? Sit down. This takes a while.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You did. Forty times.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then forty-one. First year of college. Cross country. Five miles through the woods, up the big hill, and I never breathed hard.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Last hill, I passed the whole field. Champion. They put my name on a plaque. The plaque is in a box. Somewhere.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can you still run that fast?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Sure. Sure I can. I just choose not to. It's bad for the stomach.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Race you to the pier, Boppy!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Last one there's a soggy sock!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Why is everybody walking like they're going to a fire? Slow down! My stomach is doing flips!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Boppy speed, everybody. We walk at Boppy speed.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: This is the spot. Forty years, this spot. Now everybody be QUIET.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I AM BEING QUIET.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose. Inside voice. Outside.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Shhh. Quiet on the pier, everybody. Boppy has a whole system.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom holds the tackle box. I cast. The fish comes. Nobody talks. That's the system.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Any minute now.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's been a minute. I wrote it down.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Snack. A pickled pepper settles the stomach.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee said NO peppers.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Deedee isn't here.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: BLORP.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: TATA! A FISH! A HUGE ONE! WITH A MUSTACHE!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's no perch. That's OLD IRON-GILL. I saw him in 1994! I TOLD everybody!

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. Something smells like peppers.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: MY JAR!

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: GULP. Spicy. I love it. Bye.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That was UNCALLED for!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Pickled in 1989. Nobody takes Boppy’s peppers. NOBODY.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Iron-Gill swam west with my jar, into the Whispering Marsh. Come on, we're going after him. And nobody walk fast.

lines.speaker: Soggy Sock
lines.text: Squelch. Have you seen my other sock? It looks just like me. It's ALSO angry.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, that sock has a FACE.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Marsh junk. Everything people drop out here ends up grumpy about it. Like me, at the DMV.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good. Nobody is missing. Again.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Socks. Out here. Nobody keeps track of their socks anymore.

lines.speaker: Tangle
lines.text: Snarl. Somebody cast me badly in 1997. I've been in a knot ever since. Nobody gets past ME.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Excuse me? Nobody gets past ME. That's MY line. I was saying that at Rikers before you were a knot.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good. Nobody is missing. Again.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy, you're breathing kind of hard.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'm breathing EXACTLY as hard as I want to.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We take it slow. Iron-Gill’s wake goes northwest, toward those big reeds.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The old reeds. When I was a kid we said there was a sundial back in there that told the wrong time.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Sundials can't tell the wrong time. That's not how sundials work.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's what I said.

lines.speaker: Old reeds
lines.text: Iron-Gill’s wake goes straight into the reeds. There used to be a boardwalk through here. Something big and soggy is sitting in front of it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we ask it nicely to move. Iron-Gill isn't keeping that jar.

lines.speaker: Snag
lines.text: Creak. This was a boardwalk once. Now it's MY spot. Everything catches on me here. I like it.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You're sitting on the way to Sundial Hollow. Shove over.

lines.speaker: Snag
lines.text: Make me. Slowly. I'm very heavy when wet. I'm always wet.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, it's a LOG with a BOOT.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good. Nobody is missing. Again.

lines.speaker: Old reeds
lines.text: The Snag rolls over, creaks, and drifts off into the shallows. Behind it, the old reeds lean apart around a narrow, mossy boardwalk.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A secret boardwalk. Of course there's a secret boardwalk.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Not secret. Just old. Like me. Nobody comes back here anymore.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: This is Sundial Hollow. I haven't been back here since I was nine, and it hasn't changed.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The sundial still says seven o'clock, no matter what time it is.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's the AFTERNOON. The sun is right there. Sundials can't be wrong. That's not how sundials work.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's what I said.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata! Something shiny is stuck in it!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's a gold coin, wedged right under the pointer. That's what was holding the shadow at seven. Somebody pushed this in on purpose.

lines.speaker: The sundial
lines.text: Click. The shadow swings all the way around the dial and settles on the right hour.

lines.speaker: The spillway
lines.text: Up north, the spillway gurgles, then glugs, then drains away to mud. The way to the Deep Pool is open.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It MOVED. Shadows don't move like that. I'm writing this down. In pen.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Old gold. Keep that in your pocket, Tom. Penny will want to hear about it. Penny wants to hear about everything.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Now the water has drained, and the way to the Deep Pool is open. That's where Iron-Gill goes to sulk.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The Deep Pool. Nobody has ever seen the bottom. My father said it goes all the way to Ohio.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. The old man. And his small, loud friends.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You took my jar.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: I took your jar. Forty years you sit on that pier and you never once come to visit. You only ever bring HOOKS.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: A man in a long coat stopped the sundial for me. He said if the day never ended, you'd never pack up and go home.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, he's sad! And spicy!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He's a FISH, kiddo.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom. Tackle box. We do this the old way.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Quiet on the pier, everybody.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He belches every third turn, Tom. Heal right after. When he dives, hit the water hard, or do our Tombo.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. Fine. FINE. Take your jar. It was too spicy anyway.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My jar. Still sealed. Still hot.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: And look at that. Forty years, and I finally caught Old Iron-Gill.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Technically he caught your jar, and then we caught him. I'm writing it down anyway. For proof.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Put the date. Put the time. Use the sundial. It works now.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It works because I took the coin out. A man in a long coat stops a sundial so a lonely fish can keep his company. That's a strange favor to do for a fish.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Go on, you old bucket. Catch and release. I'll come by. No hooks.

lines.speaker: Deep Pool
lines.text: Iron-Gill sinks back into the Deep Pool, burping softly. The bubbles look almost friendly.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, can we go home now? I want to tell Deedee EVERYTHING.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Everything except the pepper part.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ESPECIALLY the pepper part.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There they are! Well? Did anybody catch anything?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Old Iron-Gill. Forty years, Dee. I TOLD everybody.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nobody believed you.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I have proof. It's in my notebook. With the time. From a sundial.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee! Boppy almost ate a PEPPER! On the pier! Before LUNCH!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Did he.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Hand me my glasses. I want to look at him properly. Where ARE my glasses.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Apron pocket, Deedee!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Thank you, Rosie. Now. Let me look at him.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Almost isn't eating. Almost is fine.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Sit down, you. I made rhubarb crisp. Everybody sit. And eat SLOWLY.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Slowly. Finally. Somebody in this family gets it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Best fishing trip ever. Nobody fell in. Mostly.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I love you all to the moon and back. Now eat.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Well, well, well...

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look who flew in for my big day. I'm on a forty-minute lunch. I spent thirty of it on the Metro.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You took the train to meet the plane.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I took the train to meet the man. The plane was a bonus.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Big shoot today. BACKLOT BEDLAM. Car chases, a saloon, a fake New York. I have forty costumes on one rack, and every single one is steamed.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Also, Olivia dropped Nara at your place again. Family trip to the desert. She's been howling at your front door since nine.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we get Nara. Then I watch you be very important. I'm not joking.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Very, very important. I have a lanyard.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: A howl from 2nd Ave. Nara has spotted Tom from the porch, two whole blocks away.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: She does three laps around Tom, slams into his shins, and leans on him with all forty pounds.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hi. Hi. Yes. I know. I was gone FOREVER. It was six days.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's coming to set. I already asked. Nobody said yes, but nobody said no fast enough.

lines.speaker: Ray
lines.text: Sunset Gold Studios. Closed set. Name?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Ray, it's me. Wardrobe. I left eighty minutes ago. You waved.

lines.speaker: Ray
lines.text: I wave at everybody. That's the job. Go on in.

lines.speaker: Kiki
lines.text: TNB! TNB! The rack! Rack two! It's GONE.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Gone? It's a rack. It has wheels. It doesn't have ambitions.

lines.speaker: Kiki
lines.text: It was right there in Stage 7. Then the fog machine turned itself on, and the lights went out, and things started CLAPPING.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: I'm Dana Park, the director, and this is my first feature. Without the costumes we can't shoot, and without a shoot there's no movie.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: And the Backlot is full of little grumpy things. One of them ate a cue card. One of them is clapping at the horse.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Those sound like Friction Sprites. Grumpy little monsters, loose on a closed set.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Forty costumes. I steamed every single one. By hand. While humming.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we go get them back. Nara, stay close. This is a professional environment.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara is already sniffing the craft services table.

lines.speaker: Toni
lines.text: Plain roast chicken. No salt, no skin, no sauce. I keep it for the grips. They're also picky.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara takes it very gently. Then she inhales it. Then she sits again, in case there's more.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's never eaten anything that fast. Not even my shoe.

lines.speaker: Toni
lines.text: Here. For the road. Don't tell the grips.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The Backlot. Main Street up on the left, the Western street on the right, New York down on the left. All fake. All very expensive.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara’s ears go straight up. Something shiny is skittering across New York.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nara. NARA. Don't...

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's a closed set! She's not on the call sheet!

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara sniffs the fire hydrant. She gets VERY excited about the fire hydrant.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She peed on the hydrant. That hydrant is fiberglass. That hydrant is a PROP.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She doesn't know that. Let her have this.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: She drops something at Tom’s feet. Very proud. Very slobbery.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's a costume tag. That's MY tag. WARDROBE, RACK 2, HAND WASH ONLY. I underlined it twice.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And it smells like grape fog juice. Only Stage 7 has a fog machine, so my rack must be in Stage 7.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Good girl. Professional environment, very good girl.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Stage 7 is locked from the inside, though. And every set out here has a Sprite on it wrecking the shoot. The crew can't work like this.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we clear the Sprites off the sets, one at a time: Main Street, the Western street and New York. After that we deal with Stage 7.

lines.speaker: Cue Card Crab
lines.text: Pinch. This is MY set. I hold up the lines. Every line. I hold up this one: GO AWAY.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Those are the neatest cue cards I've ever seen. Is that calligraphy?

lines.speaker: Cue Card Crab
lines.text: ...Don't try to be nice to me. Nobody is nice to me. I'll PINCH.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Cut. Reset. Back to one. Everybody gets a touch-up.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Main Street is clear. The bank is safe. The pie is still foam.

lines.speaker: Kiki
lines.text: (on the radio) ...kkkt... Stage 7! The big door just unlocked itself! From the INSIDE! Is that bad? That feels bad.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: All three sets are clear, and Stage 7 just unlocked itself. That's where the fog came from, so that's where my rack is.

lines.speaker: Clapper Snapper
lines.text: SNAP! Scene one, take one! SNAP! I go first! Nothing happens until I clap! SNAP!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's very fast. And very loud.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's every clapper I've ever met.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Cut. Reset. Back to one. Everybody gets a touch-up.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The Western street is clear. The horse can come out of its trailer now.

lines.speaker: Kiki
lines.text: (on the radio) ...kkkt... Stage 7! The big door just unlocked itself! From the INSIDE! Is that bad? That feels bad.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: All three sets are clear, and Stage 7 just unlocked itself. That's where the fog came from, so that's where my rack is.

lines.speaker: Boom Mic Moth
lines.text: Bzzz. I hear everything on this set. Everything. Your knees click, Tom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That was UNCALLED for!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Watch the screech, babe. It shuts you right up. No skills.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Cut. Reset. Back to one. Everybody gets a touch-up.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: New York is clear. It never looked better. It's plywood.

lines.speaker: Kiki
lines.text: (on the radio) ...kkkt... Stage 7! The big door just unlocked itself! From the INSIDE! Is that bad? That feels bad.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: All three sets are clear, and Stage 7 just unlocked itself. That's where the fog came from, so that's where my rack is.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Somebody killed the work lights. And look, the catwalk is up. You only raise a catwalk when you're hiding something up there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The stage set is at the top. The rack is up there. I can smell the steamer.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The main light rig runs the catwalk motor. If I get power back to it, the catwalk comes down.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Three junction boxes. They have to come up in the right order or the dimmer pops. The rig will tell us the order.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Blue, amber, red. And one strip of gaffer tape. Okay, two. Okay, four.

lines.speaker: Soundstage 7
lines.text: The rig hums. The work lights bang on, one row at a time. Up the middle, the catwalk groans down into place.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You fixed a whole soundstage with tape.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I fix everything with tape. You know this. Your kitchen drawer knows this.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: My rack. MY RACK. All forty. Still steamed. Oh, I could cry.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: CUT! CUT! CUT! Who said you could walk onto my set? The blocking is WRONG.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: I've been on this lot for forty years, and every bad take was yelled through ME. Nobody ever gets it right.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You took the rack.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: So I took the costumes. With no costumes there's no take, and with no take there's no BAD take. It's perfect. It's my best work.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: A man in a long coat paid me to do it. One gold coin. He said a day with no takes is a day that never has to end.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. It's a megaphone in a beret. It has notes.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara growls at the megaphone. Very small growl. Very serious.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: This is a closed set. And you're not on the call sheet.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Back to one, everybody. Touch-ups.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, when it says CUT, put WARDROBE on whoever is next. When it braces, Popcorn Jump. Or just tell it GREAT TAKE. Three times.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: Fine. FINE. That’s a wrap. On me. I'm going back in the prop closet.

lines.speaker: Stage set
lines.text: The megaphone hops off the rack and rolls away under the set, muttering about lighting.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Forty. I counted. I'm going to count again. Forty.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And look. Somebody stuck a note on the steamer. "Paid in full." With a gold coin taped to it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Another gold coin, same as the one in the sundial. First he stops a sundial for a fish, and now he pays a megaphone to stop a movie.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Somebody in a long coat really wants things to stand still.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Spooky. I love it. I hate it. Help me push. This thing has four wheels and four opinions.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: The rack! The costumes! We can shoot! We're shooting! That's a WRAP on today, everybody!

lines.speaker: Kiki
lines.text: WRAP PARTY AT CRAFTY! Toni made a cake! It's shaped like a clapper! It's not clapping!

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: TNB, the studio wants you to have this. Gold-plated. It's the steamer from the lot’s very first wardrobe department.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'm going to cry. I'm not going to cry. I'm a professional. I'm crying a little.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You're a professional. A crying professional. I'm so proud of you.

lines.speaker: Dana
lines.text: And crew jackets. Wrap Party Jackets. Only the crew gets one. You're crew now. Even the dog.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You know what this whole day was? A real steam-ulating experience.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I flew three thousand miles for that pun.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Worth it?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Worth it. Every mile. But for the record? That was a CLOSED set!

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara leans on both of them. A tiny excited puddle. Nobody minds. Craft services minds a little.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A text from Amy. "Parent-teacher conference night is Thursday. Thirty parents. I need backup. Bring snacks. And bring the good uncle."

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You're the only uncle.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Which makes me the good one. By default. I'll take it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: TOM. Oh, thank goodness.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Two coffees. Both mine. Here, have one. That's how much I need you tonight.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You brought me coffee. At night. That's a cry for help.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It's conference night. Thirty parents at seven o’clock. And the school has lost its mind.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The bells ring whenever they feel like it. Every clock says a different time. And the sign-up sheet ran off.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Ran off? Like, RAN? On legs?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: On little paper legs. Mrs. Kowalski saw it. She's still upset about it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Mom. Mom. Are we going to SCHOOL? At NIGHT? That's the best thing that ever happened.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody is coming. I have a clipboard, and I'm not afraid to use it.

lines.speaker: School bell
lines.text: BRRRRRING. From inside the school. Then again. Then a little one: brring?

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori! Thank goodness. And you brought the whole family.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Principal Pruitt, my brother Tom. He's very good in a crisis. He's also very calm about it, which is annoying.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello. I hear your bells are haunted.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Not haunted. Grumpy. Thirty-one years in this building. I know the difference.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: The bells ring at random. The clocks in the hall all say different times. And the sign-up sheet got up off the table and walked into the school.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: The Cafetorium doors run on the bell system, and the bells run on the hallway clocks.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Until the clocks are right, those doors won't open, and thirty parents are on their way.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Doors don't just not open. That's not how doors work.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: So please set every clock in the hall to exactly seven o'clock. Not seven-thirty, and not six-fifty-nine. Seven.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. A school. At NIGHT. With MONSTERS, probably.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stay close, everybody. This is a professional learning environment.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Every clock in this hall says a different time.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That one says four. That one says nine. That one is going BACKWARDS. I teach time, Tom. This is personal.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata! Tata! SPARKLY FOOTPRINTS!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Little paper feet. With glitter. They go EVERYWHERE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I can read the doors. Room One is ART. Room Two is MUSIC. Room Three is the GYM.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The gym isn't a room. It's a gym. It has a number anyway.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The footprints go into all three rooms and out again, and then east to the Cafetorium. The sign-up sheet went that way.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. That's excellent detective work. Gold stars. Both of you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we clear the monsters out of Art, Music and the Gym. After each room, we set its hallway clock to seven o'clock.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: When all three are right, the Cafetorium opens.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: FOR EVERYONE, LOVE DEEDEE. That's Deedee’s handwriting! Everyone means us!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Rhubarb crisp! Deedee brings the teachers CRISP?

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Every conference night. Twelve years. It's the only reason Gary shows up.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: She never told me that. Of course she never told me that.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: To the moon and back. And apparently to the staff room.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Take some for the road. Don't tell Gary.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: DING! You're LATE! Everybody is late! I ring and I ring and nobody is ever on time!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I've never been late in my life. Not once. Not even when I was born. I was early.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: ...DING. Prove it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up! Everybody up! Walk it off. Hydrate. We go again.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, listen. The clock outside the Art room stopped spinning.

lines.speaker: Glitter Glue
lines.text: Squelch. I glued the piano. I glued the xylophone. I glued a recorder to a tuba. It's ART.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, it's SPARKLY. I love it. I hate it. I love it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can't glue a xylophone. That's not how xylophones work.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up! Everybody up! Walk it off. Hydrate. We go again.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The glitter footprints stop here! And over there. And on Tata.

lines.speaker: Dodgeball Dread
lines.text: BOING. Everybody against the wall. Nobody picks me first. Nobody EVER picks me first.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Oh, I remember you. Fourth grade. You and me. Every Friday.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy was the scariest kid in dodgeball. They had to make a rule about her.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The Gregori Rule. No throwing at teachers. It's still on the wall.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up! Everybody up! Walk it off. Hydrate. We go again.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You know I was terrified of that thing? Every Friday. That's why I threw so hard.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. You threw one at me at Thanksgiving. I was holding a pie.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You caught the pie, though.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I caught the pie.

lines.speaker: School bell
lines.text: BRRRRRING. One bell. Right on time. Then silence. The good kind.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: (on the intercom) ...ksssh... Attention, please. The Cafetorium doors are OPEN. Parents, please wait in the hall. There's something in the Cafetorium.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori’s brother, please go into the Cafetorium. Thank you. ...ksssh.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The footprints go in there. The sign-up sheet must be in there.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And the something.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: There! The sign-up sheet! On the podium!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It's covered in RED.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Click. Wrong. Wrong. Wrong. Every name on this sheet is written wrong.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Kowalski has a W. Delgado has a G. Gregori has TWO Rs, and nobody ever writes them neatly.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That's the conference sign-up sheet. Thirty parents are waiting for it.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: I have marked a hundred thousand wrong answers in this school. Every quiz, every spelling test and every crooked line.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: But nobody ever grades ME, and nobody ever writes NEAT next to MY work. So tonight I'm grading the grown-ups.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: So you took the sign-up sheet to mark it up, and you scrambled the bells and the clocks too.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: I did. I made the bells and the clocks wrong so that everybody would be late. Late is late. Points off.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: A man in a long coat gave me a gold coin for it.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: He said if the clocks never agree, conference night never has to start, and then nobody ever goes home.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, it's a PEN. With GLASSES.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I'm going to count to three, and you're going to put the sheet down. One.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's her teacher voice. I'd listen.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Everybody. Walk it off.

lines.speaker: Amy
