lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: My boarding pass changed. "BOARDING GROUP 0. FROM: LONG ISLAND. TO: NOWHERE. STATUS: LAYOVER."

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: What's a layover?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A layover is a stop in the middle of a trip. It means this trip isn't over. And neither is he.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. It's twelve oh four. Mom has been holding Sunday dinner since midnight. Everybody to the cab.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: THERE they are. Tom! The oven clock started blinking twelve oh one and I cried a little. Into the gravy. It's fine. It's seasoning.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Every clock in this house started at once. Eleven clocks. I didn't know we'd eleven clocks.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My stomach is still on midnight. My stomach is always on midnight.

lines.speaker: Aunt Ellie
lines.text: Sit. Tell me about the airport. Leave nothing out. I'll know.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: DAD!

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Hey, everybody. The lights all came back on at twelve oh one. So I came back too. I brought bread.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's store-bought.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: It's store-bought.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I'll allow it. Tonight.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: None for me, Justin. Store-bought gives me gas.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee! EVERYTHING gives you GAS!

lines.speaker: Sunday dinner
lines.text: Everybody laughs. Boppy laughs so hard he has to hold his stomach. Deedee laughs last, and longest.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Fine. One slice. For the girl who said it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A text from TNB. "babe. every clock in LA stopped at midnight. they just started again. was that you?"

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Tom writes back: "Mostly Amy." TNB sends a heart. Tom sends one back. Then another one.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mostly Amy. Put that on a shirt.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Everybody sit. Everybody. Justin, you too. Ellie, that's Boppy’s chair. Boppy, that's my chair. Boppy.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And has anybody seen my glasses? I can't read the oven.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: They're on the BUTTER, Deedee.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Of course they are. Nobody touch the butter.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Next time there's a layover, can I come?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: WE are coming. All of us. I'm already packing. In my head.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody comes next time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: To the moon and back, everybody. Eat. Deedee made everything.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: To the moon and BACK.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom! Sit. Eat. I made a crisp. Yes, I know it's nine in the morning. Do not argue.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Trust me, I was not going to argue.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A gold card came in the mail, addressed to my recliner. It says Priority Member. It’s junk mail. They send junk mail to furniture now.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Don’t throw it out, though. It feels warm. Even my knee can feel it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad. That card has a little clock on it.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Everything has a clock on it. It’s junk mail.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Don’t sign anything.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I never sign anything. I didn’t sign the mortgage. Your mother did.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The boarding pass from Gate Zero is buzzing in my pocket. Now it says: YOUR LAYOVER IS NOW BOARDING.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The man in the long coat said my layover would be announced. I think this is it. I have to go back to Gate Zero.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: A layover! Where? Never mind. Take a sweater. Actually, take two. And take the crisp.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Bring me back a pretzel. A real one. Not the airport kind.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: To the moon and back, Tom. Both ways.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom! Sit. Eat. I made a crisp. Yes, I know it's nine in the morning. Do not argue.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Trust me, I was not going to argue.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A gold card came in the mail, addressed to my recliner. It says Priority Member. It’s junk mail. They send junk mail to furniture now.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Don’t throw it out, though. It feels warm. Even my knee can feel it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad. That card has a little clock on it.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Everything has a clock on it. It’s junk mail.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Don’t sign anything.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I never sign anything. I didn’t sign the mortgage. Your mother did.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The boarding pass from Gate Zero is buzzing in my pocket. Now it says: YOUR LAYOVER IS NOW BOARDING.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The man in the long coat said my layover would be announced. I think this is it. I have to go back to Gate Zero.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: A layover! Where? Never mind. Take a sweater. Actually, take two. And take the crisp.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Bring me back a pretzel. A real one. Not the airport kind.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: To the moon and back, Tom. Both ways.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. Welcome aboard Flight Zero, nonstop to Wherever. Please stow your bags, your seatbacks, and your questions.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Flight Zero was waiting at the gate with one seat made up. A real pod seat. Somebody upgraded me, and nobody told me why.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And something in seat 5B is giggling.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Whoever is under the blanket, you’re breathing very loudly.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: BOO! We’re stowaways! Tata, what’s a stowaway?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s a person who hides on a plane they weren’t invited to.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Which is illegal. And also, apparently, a family tradition.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We weren’t hiding. We were pre-boarding. Rose got the good blanket.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You said everybody comes next time, Tata. This is next time.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s the one with the tiny planes on it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, if you tell Mom, I’m going to make a video about it. Please like and subscribe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody is subscribing to a stowaway.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: STOP THE PLANE! I don’t have a ticket. I have my running shoes, and I just chased my daughters across a whole airport.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: They ran out of the house in their socks, Tom. Wherever this plane is going, I’m going too. I’m their ride home. And I’m faster than you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody here is racing.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That’s what the person who loses says.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: Ladies and gentlemen, we are experiencing a little weather. It is not the kind with rain. Please look out the window.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The sky has a hole in it. The hole is pink. Tata, can I touch it?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No touching, please.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The plane is flying straight into it. Everybody hold on to something. Preferably each other.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. Welcome to Terminal Infinity, where it is always dusk and every flight is on time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We flew through the hole in the sky and landed at an airport that isn’t on any map.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, look out the big window. There are two tiny towns floating out there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The green one on the left is Long Island, and the orange one on the right is Los Angeles.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: They’re both inside glass, like snow globes.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Then this is the layover on your boarding pass.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s a place in between our two homes, where everything is on time and nothing is going anywhere.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can we live here? There’s a plant with a hat.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We are not living in an airport, Rose.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’re going to find whoever sent me that boarding pass. The only way on is east, down the Endless Concourse.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: There are nine gates here: Boston, Denver, Seattle, Chicago, Miami and more. Every one of them says PAUSED.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Each window is a whole town, stopped in the middle of one day. Look, that seagull still has the same fry.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Careful. Those are real towns with real people in them, even if they’re paused. Don’t lick the glass.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I wasn’t going to.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I was going to look at it with my face.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Gate Infinity is the big door at the far end. I think the man in the long coat is behind it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: But there’s a checkpoint in the middle, and somebody is standing in it.

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: Hold it. Hold it right there. Name?

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: You’re not on the list. Nobody is ever on the list. That makes you standby passengers. Congratulations, you’re number eighteen.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Who is number seventeen?

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: Me. I’ve been number seventeen since 1998, waiting for a seat. Nobody gets through this checkpoint ahead of me.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ve never been on standby in my life. I’ve been on time, or I’ve been first.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose, he has a paddle that says STANDBY and he thinks it’s a weapon.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stay behind me. If he sends someone to the back of the line, we’ll get them right back.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody okay? Good. He’s a clipboard with legs.

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: ...Seventeen. Somebody called seventeen. Was that me?

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: It was me. I’m on the plane. I’m on THE PLANE.

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: ...Seventeen. Somebody called seventeen. Was that me?

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: It was me. I’m on the plane. I’m on THE PLANE.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. Flight Zero from Los Angeles has arrived at the Jet Bridge. Welcome to the layover. Please do not feed the dog the pretzels.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara sees Tom. Nara sees EVERYTHING that is not Tom disappear.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hi. Hi, bean. Yes. I know. You were so brave on the plane.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hey, babe. A gold boarding pass turned up on the loft door this morning, with my name and Nara’s on it. So we got on the plane.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The airline lost my bag, found Nara, and upgraded us both.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You flew through the hole in the sky too.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I flew through a pink hole in the sky with a dog on a pillow. It was fine. There was a ceramic pot on the drinks cart that was kind of incredible.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Hi! I’m Grace. I’m nine.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I know exactly who you are. Tom shows me all your videos. You’re very good at telling people to subscribe.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Thank you. Subscribe.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m Rose. I’m six. I’m on a longboard.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s my longboard.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s ours now.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara licks Grace’s glitter nails, one at a time. She seems to feel it’s a type of review.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: So you’re TNB. The boyfriend. We finally meet in person.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And you’re the sister. The runner. I’ve heard a lot.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ve heard nothing, which means he’s been saving you for a special occasion.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I can fix a handle or fire a vase. What are you good at?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everything, and quickly. I think we’re going to get along.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay, everybody. It’s always dusk here and nobody has slept, so I’m calling a sleepover before we go any farther.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We have a blanket, a dog, and nine hours of dusk.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Tom, build the fort. I’ll make the snacks.

lines.speaker: Lost and Found
lines.text: The door was never locked. It just said BACK IN FIVE MINUTES for so long that nobody tried it.

lines.speaker: Lost and Found
lines.text: Inside: a counter, a brass bell, and shelves that go up past the ceiling. Every item has a little gold clock tied to it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can I ring the bell?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Gently.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I rang it gently. It rang back less gently.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. Every single thing here has a tag. A blue mitten. A trombone. A birthday hat. A retainer.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Nobody has claimed the retainer in my family since 2011. That’s not related. Moving on.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: These are all things people left behind when they got to the good part of a trip. A mitten from the best snow day. A hat from the best party.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: They didn’t want the good part to end, so they left a piece of it behind and never came back for it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And somebody collected all of it. Every tag has the same little gold clock that’s on my coins.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, the Lost Luggage monsters from the Concourse are all in here. And they’re all being very polite.

lines.speaker: Lost and Found
lines.text: A ledger on the counter. UNCLAIMED: 4,017,311 ITEMS. CLAIMED: 0.

lines.speaker: Lost and Found
lines.text: The last line, in gold ink: THE ONLY WAY TO LEAVE SOMETHING SAFE IS TO NEVER COME BACK FOR IT.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That is the saddest thing I have ever read. And I read my sister’s diary.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I don’t have a diary. I have a drawing of a dog.

lines.speaker: Lost and Found
lines.text: Under the bell, a card in the same gold ink as the one at Gate Zero:

lines.speaker: Lost and Found
lines.text: FOUND: ONE TOM. HELD FOR PICKUP. NO RUSH.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...He’s been holding a spot here for me. Not for my bag. For me. He wants me to stay.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That’s either the nicest thing I’ve ever heard or a threat.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Both, probably. That’s how the good ones are.

lines.speaker: Long coat
lines.text: Hello, Tom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re the man in the long coat. You were in the school parking lot, and on the jet bridge at Gate Zero. You handed out the coins.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: My name is Julian Vance. I’m a gate agent, in a way. I have stood at every gate that ever closed.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: Eight times I gave something lonely a coin and a promise, and eight times your family talked it out of both. Thank you for flying nowhere, Tom.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: You are very hard to stop.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You stopped our clocks. You stopped MY clock.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: I stopped every town on Earth at its happiest afternoon. A birthday that never ends, or the last day of summer.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: In those towns nobody is ever sad, and nobody is ever late.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It should always be this afternoon. Babe, that’s what Mr. Washington kept saying when the purple smog came down.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: That was my first try at your street. It would not hold still.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: Only Long Island and Los Angeles kept moving, because you kept flying between them.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: Every flight you took moved them along a little, and I was never quick enough to stop you.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: That is why I sent for you. If you stay here, your two towns will stop as well, and then everyone, everywhere, is safe.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Paused isn’t happy. Paused is stuck.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The seagull has had that fry for a hundred years. He’s not happy. He’s hungry.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You told the Mirrorball it could have one dance forever. You told the Last Call it could have midnight forever. They weren’t bad. They were lonely.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I think you are too.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have a vase in the kiln in Los Angeles. It’s been in there a long time. It’s going to crack.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s what happens when you leave something at its best. It doesn’t stay good. It just stays.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: Maybe. But it stays safe. That is all I have ever wanted for anyone.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: I want everyone safe, in the good part, forever. So come in, all of you, and stay. Nobody here has ever been lost.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s the nicest offer anyone has ever made me. And I’ve had the boarding pass for it in my pocket this whole time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No, thank you. We have a connection to make.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: ...Then I can’t let you leave. I’ll have to make the last announcement.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: Someone has to.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He lifts his hat. Behind his head, the big door’s gold clock spins, and every flap in the terminal clicks at once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The departures board beside the door unfolds, stands up on two legs, and steps out.

lines.speaker: Julian Vance
lines.text: FINAL CALL.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Here’s the plan. Tom up front, girls with me. If that board calls your name, don’t sit there. Move.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose, when it calls you, move. Don’t stop to look at anything.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I won’t look at anything.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ...I looked at one thing.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: If somebody gets called and can’t move, I’ll walk them on. And if we need a friend in a hurry, wave to the bench.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody okay? It calls one of us every turn. Move before it goes again, or Tom will walk you on.

lines.speaker: FINAL CALL
lines.text: ...ON TIME. ON TIME. ON TIME.

lines.speaker: FINAL CALL
lines.text: It’s fine. They’re all on time. I am not.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Nobody is cancelling you. You just never got a boarding pass. Here. Take mine.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Something is dropping out of the gate clock. A gold coin, with a little clock face. Number nine.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s warm. This is one of the old gold coins he bought up on Long Island. He was using it to hold that gate shut.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And Vance is gone. He slipped away while we were busy with his board.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. Attention, passengers. The departures board has been updated.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. LONG ISLAND: CLOSED. LOS ANGELES: NOW BOARDING.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, look at the window. The little green town is changing color. It’s turning amber, like a caution light.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He closed Long Island. He couldn’t make us stay, so he stopped our home instead.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is Deedee okay?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’m calling her. I’m calling her right now.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s ringing. It’s just ringing. Mom always picks up. Mom picks up on the FIRST ring. She picks up before it rings.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sit down. Everybody. Deep breath.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad’s in his recliner. Mom has the crisp. They’re fine. They’re probably fine.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hey. We’ll go get them. Whatever he did, we’ll fix it. Things come apart. I fix things.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll go get them. We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Which one is Los Angeles?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Los Angeles is the orange one. It’s the only gate still open, so that’s the way we have to go. We’ll find a road back to Long Island from there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And it’s where Nara and TNB live. It’s home. Our other home.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. Attention, passengers. Los Angeles is now boarding. All other gates remain closed.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The gold clock on the big door finally has hands. They’re pointing at 3, 4, 6, 8.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s my house number in Los Angeles. The door is going to open onto my street.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The door knows where you live? That’s so creepy. I love it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Home. Okay. Good. I have a very good couch and a very bad idea of what’s in the fridge.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara hears the word home. Nara is already pressed against the door, vibrating.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody together. Nobody gets left behind in the layover. That’s the only rule.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That’s two rules. Together, and nobody gets left.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: They’re the same rule, Grace.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dog on a leash. Girls on the buddy system. Here we go.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Jefferson Park. Same jacarandas, same lemon tree, same wood door.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nothing is paused here. The sprinklers are even on.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It smells like lemons. And a little bit like a burrito.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s the lemon tree and Doña Carmen’s. Welcome to 3468.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, you live in a real grown-up house. With flax.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: What’s flax?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The red grass by the steps. It looks like it’s waving.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s waving at ME.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Wood door. A welcome mat in Japanese. Not one thing out of place.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ve known you thirty-some years, and I pictured a pile of laundry and a gaming chair.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB is the reason nothing is out of place.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’m the reason there are coasters.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara checks the front gate. A squirrel is on the fence. Nara loses her entire mind.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Come in. I’ll show you where I live. Wipe your paws, Nara. And mind the sourdough.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. TATA. There’s a jar. It’s bubbling. It’s ALIVE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s Bready Mercury. He’s nine years old, he’s flown Delta One, and he’s the only one in this house who gets fed on time.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You named your bread Mercury? Like the planet?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Like the singer. He’s a showman. He rises on command.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can he do a trick?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He rises. Every day. Without being asked. It’s the best trick anybody in this house does.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I do a trick where I turn a lump into a bowl.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You do. Yours is better. Don’t tell Bready.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. There’s a picture of us. On the wall. In the nice frame.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: There’s one of me with a sandwich. It’s my best side.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s the wall I walk past every morning. Before work. Before coffee.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I say good morning to the two of you.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Every morning?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every morning. Rose usually says it back. In my head.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I said it back just now. Good morning, Tata.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Good morning, Rose.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So this is your house.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s yours too. I mean it. A snow globe called Long Island, and a house called this one. Both. Always both.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom. That wall is the nicest thing I’ve seen in a house in years.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s an Ikea frame. Don’t make it weird.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s a very nice Ikea frame.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara has climbed onto the couch. This is not allowed. She looks right at Tom. It is allowed.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Next stop, the loft. Everybody’s coming. I’ll show you where I break things on purpose.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: This is it. The loft. Kiln, wheel, and a lot of clay in places clay shouldn’t be.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s so many mugs.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can I touch the clay?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Rose. Come here. Wet hands. Sit. Put your thumb in the middle. Don’t push. Just open it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s a hole.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s a bowl. It just doesn’t know yet.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Mine is leaning.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Leaning is a style. It’s called Pisa.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He taught my six-year-old to center clay in four minutes. I’ve been trying to get her to center her cereal for two years.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Clay doesn’t move. Cereal moves.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: So. Tom. Tell me one thing he does when he thinks nobody is watching.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He checks the front door three times before bed. Tells me it’s for the raccoons.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He did that at nine. He told Mom it was so Chester couldn’t get out.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Who’s Chester?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Our cat. Chester never once tried to get out.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The first night I fired the big kiln alone, it was three in the morning. I looked up and he was standing in the doorway. With a thermos and a blanket. Just in case.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That is exactly him. He’s been standing in doorways with a thermos since he was nine.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He thinks I didn’t see him. I fired a second kiln so he’d have a reason to stay.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. I like you. Don’t tell him.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He’s standing right behind you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I was looking at a mug.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s a very nice mug.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Look! I made a bowl! It has a hat! The hat is a lump!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s the best bowl in the loft. It goes in the kiln tonight. You can pick it up when we’re all home safe.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Love it. Love the block. Love the lemons. So many lemons. What is that, a jacaranda? Needs less.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me. Who are you?

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I’m Marlowe. Monochrome Marlowe. I work for Mr. Vance, and I fix places.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: This place has too much going on: too much color, too many porches, and a dog doing something on a lawn.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara, offended, does it again. On purpose.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s a neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: That’s the problem with a neighborhood. Notes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He lifts a clipboard. The top page says NOTES: LESS. He snaps his fingers.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He took the pink off the jacaranda!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can’t just take the pink!

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I can take the pink, the yellow, and the music out of that window. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe. Quiet sells.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I have twelve kids in my room who’ve had harder mornings than you. You don’t scare me. Colors back, please.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I don’t put things back. I take notes. Anyway, Mr. Prime will handle the intersection. Do take a look at the traffic. It’s very stationary.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He walks off into the grey, humming a jingle that never resolves.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He’s draining the color out of the whole block. And he did something worse. Look at Mr. Washington. He’s not moving.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He’s inside something. It’s see-through and yellow, like the honey bear.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s the same color the Long Island gate turned, Tata. That’s amber. It’s what the bugs are stuck in, in my rock book.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s hard like glass, but it’s warm. Babe, it’s as warm as a mug right out of the kiln.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He’s all right in there. He’s just stopped, right in the middle of one second.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: This is what Vance told us he does. He stops people at a nice moment so that nothing ever changes. This is what it looks like up close.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: When that man took the color and the music, the warm part of the day had nowhere to go. So it set hard, right around him. That’s what amber is: warmth that got stuck.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Doña Carmen’s is right there, and the Alvarez house is down 2nd. If it happened to him, it happened to them. We check on the neighbors first.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And if amber is warmth that got stuck, maybe we can get it moving again.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Doña Carmen turned into candy.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She’s in amber too, frozen right in the middle of a sentence.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: She’s still pointing at the volcano.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s warm, same as Mr. Washington’s. I don’t think we can break it, and I don’t think we should. If amber is warmth that got stuck, we have to give the warmth somewhere to go.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Warmth. We’re good at warmth. Something warm from outside the amber might get it flowing again. Everybody find the warmest thing in the room.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The comal! The pupusas!

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Tom lifts a pupusa off the comal. It’s still hot. Steam is coming off it, in a room where nothing else is moving.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Doña Carmen. It’s Tom. Nobody on this block has ever left your door hungry. We’re here to eat. Please wake up.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara sits at Carmen’s feet, tail wagging in a perfect circle, and sneezes on the amber.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A crack runs up the amber like sugar glass. Then another. Then it falls away in warm gold flakes.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: ...and THEN I told the man, the loroco is not optional. Tom! When did you get here? Why is everything so quiet?

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: Where did my pupusas go?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You were frozen in amber for a little while. A man in a grey suit took the color off the block, and all the warmth set hard around you. Your own pupusa got it moving again.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: I was what? I had a whole sentence. I lost the sentence. It was a good sentence.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: So that’s the rule. You can’t crack amber. You warm it up with something the person loves.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A man in a grey suit did it. His name is Marlowe.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: That man stood on my step and said my sign was “too busy.” I said the sign is busy because the food is good.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: Go next door. The Alvarez house. They didn’t get any pupusas today. Take these. Feed the children first. The grown-ups will pretend they’re not hungry.

lines.speaker: Daisy
lines.text: Tom! Tom! Everybody stopped! Abuela stopped in the middle of saying NO!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. The whole family is frozen in amber, same as Doña Carmen. Marlowe’s grey got in through the front door.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Save the pupusas for when they wake up. Warmth isn’t only food. Heat is just movement. When the girls can’t sleep, we run. Nobody stays stuck next to somebody who’s moving.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You mean...

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody up. Girls, with me. We’re running laps around the kitchen table.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Run with us, Mommy!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap one! Knees up, Rose!

lines.speaker: Don Beto
lines.text: ...and that is a FOUL! That is a foul! Who has the remote?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap two! Grace, don’t look at the camera!

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: Why is there a woman running around my table? Why is it a good idea? It’s a very good idea.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap three! Everybody on the last one!

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: ...NO. I said no. Why is everyone in my kitchen? Is that a mother running laps with two little girls?

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: ...Okay. That one can stay.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Pupusas next door, laps in here. Anything warm enough gets the amber moving. Good to know. I have a feeling we’re going to need it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That wasn’t a lap. That was a Tombo. Run With Us, Mommy. Amy, Grace and Rose, together.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: Take lemons. Take ALL the lemons. Every yard in this city has too many and somebody always leaves them on my step.

lines.speaker: Daisy
lines.text: Is it okay if I say that was the best thing that has ever happened in our kitchen?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It was the best thing in OUR kitchen too. We don’t even have a kitchen table. We have a counter.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Look at that. You put the neighbors back. Very warm. Very busy. Very much not what I asked for.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The rest of the colors too, please. All of them.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes. This intersection has no flow. Let me introduce our new Head of Traffic.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Mr. Prime! Please give them a moment to rethink the neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s the biggest car in the WORLD.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every light on the block is red. Every single one.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. Its headlights are pointed at the ground. It looks sad.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: It’s not angry. It’s stuck. Stuck is very quiet, and Mr. Vance likes quiet. Do be quick. The notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: If it’s stuck, maybe it just needs somewhere to go. Kindness first. Hit it if it hits back.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Here’s the plan. I stay with the girls. If anybody needs a break, sit on a couch or a bench and we’ll swap.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody gets run over. I’ll step in front of anyone who needs it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody okay? Good. It floors Rush Hour every third turn, so we heal before, not after.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: ...SigAlert cleared. Merging left. I’m sorry. Everybody was in my lane.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s fine. Nobody was in your lane. You were in everybody’s. Take the exit.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The green lamp just popped off the traffic light. It’s still warm, and it’s humming.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The pink is back! The jacaranda has its pink back!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And the music is back in the window.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: ...and that is why you never trust a Tuesday. Hm? Why is everybody looking at me? Did I fall asleep? Again?

lines.speaker: Larry
lines.text: I’m blowing leaves. The leaf landed. It LANDED. Thirty years I’ve waited. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Love it. Hate it. Love it. Notes withdrawn.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I’ll be Downtown, at the Movie Palace. Come by. I’ll have notes for the rest of the family.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You work for Vance, and Vance closed Long Island. My mother isn’t answering her phone. Where is she?

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Long Island is under glass now, you know. Mr. Vance put a dome over it. It’s very safe. Your mother is in her kitchen, making a crisp.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: She’s been making the same one for hours.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Tell me how to get in.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He just told us something he shouldn’t have.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He said Long Island is under glass. So Vance sealed it inside a dome, with your mom and dad in it. We’ll have to go under the glass, or around it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The Long Island gate turned amber, Tata. Is Deedee stuck like Doña Carmen was?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Maybe. And if she is, we know how to fix it now. We bring her something warm.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal and Sol know every road between here and there. We’ll start at Sol’s cab stand.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll get them back. We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sol. Vance put a glass dome over Long Island, and my parents are inside it. Sal always says you two know every road there is.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Is there a way under?

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Tom. Sit. Not that chair. That chair is Sal’s. I keep it warm for him out of spite.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Okay. Sal and I are cousins. You know that. What you don’t know is what we do between airport runs.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Is it crimes?

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: We carry letters. For eleven years we’ve run mail between Long Island and Los Angeles in the trunks of our cabs.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Nobody ever opened a bag, and nobody ever asked why two cab companies need a hundred sacks of stamps.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You’ve been running a secret mail route.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: A dispatch network. We call it the Network. We never came up with a better name.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Sol, come in. It’s Sal, calling from inside the dome. Cab seven says hi. She’s fine. She’s the only thing in town that’s still moving.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Sal. I have Tom, his sister, two nieces, a boyfriend and a dog in my lobby. Say hi.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Tommy! It’s quiet in here. Even the clocks are quiet. Your mother’s in the kitchen. Don’t panic. She’s fine. She just won’t stop baking.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal. Can you get me in?

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I’m under the dome with a shovel and a very worried shopkeeper. I can’t get out. But I can dig toward you.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: There’s a way in, and it’s called the Sub-Rail. Sal and I have been boring a tunnel under the Layover from both coasts, as a hobby.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: It was supposed to open in 2031. The two halves meet in the middle, right under the dome.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You built a transcontinental subway. As a hobby.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: We got a very good deal on a drill.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: But our drill stopped answering when the dome came down. Something put a chip in it, and now it’s loose in the tunnel. Be careful of the Worm.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The worm.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: The drill. We call her the Dual-Coast Drill. The kids at the depot call her the Worm. She doesn’t love it.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: I need two dispatchers to stay here on the radio and read the tunnel map to the team.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I’m extremely good at being in charge.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m in charge of snacks.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. Dispatch is the most important job in the building. If Sol says stay, you stay.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Copy.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Copy copy.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Sol. I am leaving my children with a cab driver.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Thirty years. Never lost a passenger. Found two in the trunk. Both were fine.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Somehow that is not comforting.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll be on the radio the whole way. Grace, you’re the voice. Rose, you’re the snacks.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Snacks are critical infrastructure.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB. Nara. Amy. With me. We go down.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have my thermos. I’m always ready for a tunnel.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara has never been this ready for anything. She is already at the Metro stairs, vibrating.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Out the door, the Metro stairs on the boulevard. Past the turnstile, there’s a door that says EMPLOYEES ONLY. That’s you. You’re employees now.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: EMPLOYEES ONLY. A platform under the boulevard. And a tunnel.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have ridden every line in this city. I didn’t know this one existed. I’m a little bit offended.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. Radio check. Say “over.”

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Over.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: At the END, Tata. You say it at the end of what you say.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I said it at the end. It was the only thing I said.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Snack check! Check your pockets! I put a pretzel in your left one!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...There’s a pretzel in my left pocket.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Tom! Good. Okay. Before you go in, I have to tell you something, and I have to say it fast, because Penny made me promise.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nickel. You’re shaking.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: For years, a man in a long coat bought gold coins from Penny’s shop and from mine. He paid double, and he never took his hat off.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Julian Vance. Those are the coins he handed to every lonely thing we met.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: We didn’t know. We thought he was a collector. We took the money. And we kept the best coins in the back, in case he ever paid triple.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Penny called on the Network from under the dome. She said, “Tell Tom we’re sorry.” And then she said, “The drawer is under the counter.”

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: There are eleven coins left between us, the last of the old gold. They were supposed to be our retirement.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Why bring them?

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Sal says gold remembers being warm. Amber is warmth that got stuck, so maybe warm gold can melt a door in it. That’s what Sal says. I don’t know.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: He’s a cab driver.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re giving up your retirement.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: I’m giving up a drawer. It’s the best drawer I ever had. Go. I’ll bring them down behind you. Sol’s driving me to the second mile marker and making me run.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You don’t have to do this.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Yes, I do. Somebody gave me a shop. I’d like to be somebody who gave something back.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The tracks run east. We follow the rails.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Stay together. Nobody falls behind. I’ll be counting.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re at mile marker one thousand two hundred and fifty. But the tunnel is forty feet long. Is that normal?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The sign says halfway. I’m choosing to believe the sign.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, did you see the stone in the doorway? It’s STANDING. I think it’s the bouncer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re breaking up. Say... over... Tata?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata? I can’t hear the... Tata? Tata?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace? Rose? The radio’s gone. It’s not static. It’s just gone.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: THIS IS A QUIET CAR.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara barks. Nothing comes out. She tries again. Nothing. She looks at her own mouth, deeply offended.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Noise is a leak. Families are the loudest leak I have ever measured.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Who are you?

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s the second time today somebody has told me quiet is safe. Marlowe said it too.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. We are a very good team. Please lower your voices.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We’re being pretty quiet right now.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: You are breathing audibly.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I teach kids for a living. I know what a person sounds like right before they say “be quiet.” You’re in the wrong tunnel.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: I have given the Drill a chip. It no longer digs toward a place. It digs toward the noise. Please observe the quiet. Goodbye.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He left the quiet on. Is anybody else’s ears ringing?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The chip makes the Drill dig toward noise. So we make a lot of noise, all together, and it’ll come to us.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ve been trying to get Rose to use her indoor voice for six years. I’m glad somebody finally wants her outdoor one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: This cavern is the middle of the tunnel. That wall of amber is the bottom of the dome over Long Island.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And there’s a hole in the dirt exactly the width of a drill.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That is the biggest drill I have ever seen.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s a Dual-Coast Drill. They went with the budget model. I can tell by the bolts.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s not charging. It’s digging in place. Round and round.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Its lamps are pointed at the amber. Like it wants to dig through and can’t.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s been drilling at that wall for years. Nobody told it to stop.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara sits very still. She has never seen anything so large that wanted so little.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Be kind to it first, and only hit it if it hits back. Amy, you heal. TNB, I’ll go for the hush chip. Everybody else, make some noise.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody okay? Good. It brings the roof down every third turn, so we heal before, not after.

lines.speaker: Drill Worm
lines.text: ...Bit’s down. Engine’s off. I wasn’t going anywhere. I was just digging in.

lines.speaker: Drill Worm
lines.text: I’m sorry about the roof.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s fine. Nobody’s mad at a drill. They’re mad at whoever put a chip in it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A little grey cube just popped out of its side. That’s the chip HUSH-9 put in it. It’s very quiet.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Not anymore.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: TATA! We can hear you! Sol says the radio is back! I ate a snack for you!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re loud and clear. What happened? Say over. At the END.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We took care of it. Over.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: See? You can do it.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Tom! Sol drove me to the second mile marker and made me run. I have never been so tired and so right.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Eleven coins. Mine are in this bag. Penny’s are on the other side of that wall.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The amber is clear on one side. There’s a pocket behind it. Two people are in it. One of them is waving a shovel.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: (through the glass) TOMMY! Over here! Hi! Don’t hug the amber, it’s sticky!

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: (through the glass) Tom! I’m so sorry! Nickel, hold up the drawer! I’ve got mine!

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Eleven coins. Hers and mine. On three.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: (through the glass) One. Two. Don’t think about the interest. Three.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The coins glow, and then they run. Gold down the glass like honey. The amber sighs and opens. Right at the height of a door.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: It worked! Gold remembers being warm! I told you! Nobody ever believes the cab driver!

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: Nickel.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Penny.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: I was saving for a boat.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: You don’t know how to drive a boat.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: That’s why it was a savings.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Tommy. Sol and I started this tunnel in 2011 with a shovel and a very good deal on a drill. I never thought anyone would walk through it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal. You’re the reason I got home.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I’m a cab driver. That’s the whole job.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: Tom. I’m sorry. I sold him the coins. I took the money and I didn’t ask.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You gave back the best drawer you ever had. We’re square.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: It was a very good drawer.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Can I say something? I’ve spent a lot of time fixing mugs somebody dropped. You don’t get the mug back. You get a better mug, with a gold line where it broke.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: That’s a very nice way to say it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s called kintsugi. It’s also called Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: TNB. You fought like somebody who’s done it his whole life.

lines.speaker: TNB

lines.text: Then it doesn’t get past us. Dad said so.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’m here, babe.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara plants her feet in the grass and growls at a grey man with a sun behind his head.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Up. We are not done. Breathe. Then we go again.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Up. We are not done. Breathe. Then we go again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The amber goes out of him all at once. Nobody cheers. There is no song. There is only the wind going through the Square.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I wanted it quieter. I only ever wanted it quieter.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Look at them. LOOK.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I didn’t want it like this.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody does. That is what he counts on.

lines.text: Mom. Dad.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s warm. Amy. It’s still a little warm.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Then they’re not gone.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: They’re not gone.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Then we get them back.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Thank you for the photograph. It is perfect. I would like to keep it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Give them back.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Nobody leaves, Tom. That is what a photograph is for. If you want them, you know the building. Downtown. Sixty floors. Do come up. I will leave the light on.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: TOMMY! He’s closing glass over the whole town! I have the girls in the cab! GET IN!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy. TNB. Nara. Run.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad. Keep her warm. I’m coming back.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Vance sealed Long Island inside a snow globe and reeled it up into the sky, with Mom and Dad still standing in the Square.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal drove us out through the Sub-Rail with the meter off. Nobody has said anything since the tunnel.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Are they cold?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No, Rose. They’re warm. I checked.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Then it’s not forever. It’s just a long time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s just a long time.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Vance said we know the building: sixty floors, in downtown Los Angeles. That’s where he took them.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: We rest tonight, and tomorrow we go up.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Downtown. The tallest thing on the boulevard that wasn’t there on Monday. Sixty floors of glass, and every clock in it says 4:59.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That’s the building. That’s where he is.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We’re coming. All of us. I already told Rose. She’s packing.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I packed a pretzel. And a second pretzel, for Deedee.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. It’s sixty floors. It’s going to be hard and strange and not fair.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We know. That’s why we’re coming.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. Here’s how we do it. We split into two teams of three. Grace, Rose and I take the stairs.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy, TNB and Nara go in through the service ducts to the Archive on floor thirty.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Divide and conquer. I like it. I also like not being on the stairs.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara does not like stairs. Nara is, however, extremely good at breaking glass.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: And I get to hit something. Good.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: I’ll keep the meter off and the engine on. Go get your folks, Tommy.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The tower goes up past the top of the screen. The doors at the bottom are glass, and they are glowing like a lit window at dinnertime.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s so tall. Tata, it’s TALLER than the Starlite.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lobby is all glass and no people. Every clock says 4:59. The second hands are shaking in place, like they are trying very hard.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s so clean. Nobody lives here. Nobody even touched the floor.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: There’s a plant. It looks scared.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Floor directory says the stairs are on the east side. Twenty-eight flights.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Twenty-eight? That’s a leg day AND an arm day.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The lifts are locked. We take the stairs to thirty. Amy, TNB and Nara meet us up there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Landing thirty. A huge glass door with a gold lock the size of a dinner plate. The counter over it says LOCKS ENGAGED 6 OF 6.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Six locks. Six of something. I don’t like that.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom, this is Amy. We’re in the service ducts. I can hear glass. A lot of glass. There’s a little hatch on your landing, it should open on the Archive.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Found it. Staff only. Somebody wrote HE IS OBVIOUSLY STAFF under it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That’s TNB’s handwriting. Go through. Girls hold the landing.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Holding the landing! Holding it! Holding!

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Attention. A collection has been disturbed. Six exhibits are no longer on file.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: This is unfortunate. This is not a problem. The Archivist is not unkind. The Archivist is only thorough.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Floors 2 to 30 are now unlocked for your convenience. The express lift has been withdrawn. Please use the stairs. All of them. The Archivist will be waiting at the top.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Withdrawn. The lift has been WITHDRAWN. Tom. Did he just challenge me to a stair race?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I don’t think he knows what he just did.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The seal door swings open on its own. The stairwell goes on. Twenty-nine more floors, straight up, in a glass tube.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You and me. Landing to landing. Loser buys dinner.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy, we have a deadline. We have a tower. We have two grandparents made of stone.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Which is why I’m going to win this.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I’m calling it. On my mark. Mark!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m the finish line!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’m not running. I’m carrying the thermos. Somebody has to.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Floor fifty-nine. We hit the vault door at exactly the same time. Amy’s forehead and mine, a quarter inch apart.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That was MINE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It was a tie.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tie means nobody won. Tie means I lost. Rematch. Later. After.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: After.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Vault. One plinth, one snow globe, and a view of Los Angeles at 4:59 PM, golden and perfect and completely still.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. It’s the Square. It’s in there. That’s Deedee. That’s BOPPY.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: They’re so small. They’re okay. They’re holding hands.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stay behind me. All of you.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Thank you for the six exhibits. The collection is, for the first time, incomplete. I find that I do not like it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re the Archivist.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: I am what Mr. Vance keeps when he wants a thing never to change. I file. I label. I hold. It is all I was made to do. It is a very good job.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You froze the pierogi man for thirty years.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Thirty-one. He was very happy. I made sure of it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s the single saddest thing I have ever heard a lens say.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Please hold still. This will not hurt. Nothing will, ever again.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Everyone up. We have a lens to break. Breathe. Then we go again.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Everyone up. We have a lens to break. Breathe. Then we go again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The amber lens cracks across the middle. The cold one goes dark. For one second, the whole building holds its breath.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: I was only... keeping them safe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. They were never yours to keep.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: What does one do... with a day that is allowed to end?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: You eat dinner. Then you go to sleep. Then it’s morning.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: That sounds... sufficient.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. The globe.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The snow globe on the plinth lifts an inch off the glass. The gold cable above it goes tight. It is going up.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Thank you for the tour, Tom. Thank you for the Archive. It was very nearly complete.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Floor sixty is for family. Come up when you are ready. I have kept your parents very warm.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom. Dad. We’re coming. We’re coming.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody breathe. We rest. Then we go to the top.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A gold lift door stands open at the north wall. No call button. A brass plate: FLOOR 60. BY INVITATION.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The pinnacle lift opens without a sound. There is no button inside, no floor number. The walls are mirrors, and every one of us is in them.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody in. Nobody lags behind. Nobody gets left on this floor.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. I’m scared. I’m also coming. Both of those are true at the same time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s exactly the right amount of both.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I brought a pretzel for Deedee. It’s a little bit squished.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Squished is fine. I fix squished things for a living.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stay behind me. All of you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The lift opens on a round room made of clock. Gold thread runs floor to ceiling, thousands of strands, humming. In the middle stands a loom the size of a house. In front of it, a man in a long coat has his back to us. His hat is on.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. Thank you for coming. Everyone, please, come in. Mind the threads. They are all somebody’s afternoon.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Where are my parents.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Warm. Downstairs, on a plinth, under glass. Exactly as you left them. I want you to understand I have taken very good care of them.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: They’re STONE.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: They are safe. There is a difference. I had to have it explained to me, too.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Are you the man who took all the coins?

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I am the man who gave them out. Gold remembers being warm.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: A coin can hold one warm moment still, for as long as something lonely is willing to hold the coin.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. I fix things for a living. Whatever this is, it’s structurally unsound.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Nothing is the same twice, Mr. TNB. You mend a cup, and it is a mended cup. I would like every cup to stay unbroken.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s not how cups work.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. You know why I wanted you. Two places that kept moving, and one man flying between them. You are not a traveler. You are the thread. If you stop, they stop. If you stay, they stay.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I will not hurt you. I will not hurt anyone. I will only finish the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No, thank you. We have a connection to make.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I know. That is why this is so hard.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The threads of the Loom lean. All of them, all at once, like a field in the wind. They gather into the brass lens at the end of his arm.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: The Ray unwrites whatever it touches. It is very gentle. They will not remember being sad. Mrs. Gregori. Mr. TNB. Grace. Rose. Hold hands, please.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Over my dead body.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: That will not be necessary. That is not even on the table.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Girls. Amy. TNB. Nara. Behind me.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara presses herself against the back of Tom’s legs and does not make a sound. She is very good at this.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He adjusts his glasses. He has done it before every hard thing, his whole life. Then he raises one hand, palm out, and takes one step forward.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No touching, please.

lines.speaker: Floor 60
lines.text: Tom steps into the Ray and takes all of it. Where he was standing, there is a small warm light, hanging in the air at about the height of his glasses.

lines.speaker: Floor 60
lines.text: Then there is not.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. TATA.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He was right there. He was RIGHT there.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara walks to the exact spot where Tom was standing, lies down on it, and does not move.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom. Tom, answer me. I’m not doing this. I’m not doing this.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Tom.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: That was not in the model.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: The Ray was written for five. He took all of it. I did not think anyone would step into it. I have never once seen anyone step into it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Give him back.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I cannot. The Loom does not hand back. I only know how it keeps.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: He is not destroyed. The Ray unwrites the story of a thing. Somewhere he is still a man with a thermos. The Loom simply does not have a place to put him.

lines.speaker: Floor 60
lines.text: The Loom shudders. Every thread in it goes white. The Ray has nowhere left to go, and a wave of light rolls out from the place Tom stood.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: That wave will carry you home. It goes to the place he is from. Hold on to something.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: We’re not leaving without him!

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: You are not leaving. You are being sent. That is a different thing.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. The wave put us down on Second Avenue, in front of Tom’s house. And it’s somehow morning.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is Tata coming?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He said we always make our connection. So he will.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I know my brother. He’s going to turn up late, a little annoyed, with a full explanation, and ask if anybody ate.

lines.text: His thermos is on the porch rail. He left it out for the cat.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is the cat going to be okay?

lines.text: The cat is fine. The cat is always fine. The cat isn’t even his.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. Okay. Plan. Mom and Dad are stone. Tom is somewhere the Loom couldn’t put him.

lines.text: And there’s exactly one thing in this city that never forgets where things go.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s been eleven hours. I’ve made coffee four times. I haven’t drunk any of it. That’s not like me.

lines.text: Plan. Mom and Dad are stone. Tom is somewhere the Loom doesn’t have a place for.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: And there’s one place in this city that keeps everything nobody could put anywhere.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The post office. We already said that.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Nara found it first.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara is sitting very straight in front of Tom’s mailbox, and she is staring into the slot. She has not blinked. A thin gold light is coming out of the slot, like a sleeping lamp.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s not a regular mailbox. That’s a mailbox that’s thinking about something.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s his. It’s the mailbox at the bottom of his steps, where his bills and my birthday cards go. It’s warm.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: If you drop a letter in a mailbox and it goes nowhere... where does it go?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Down. I think it goes down.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Vance said the Loom has no place to put him. So maybe he ended up where undelivered things go. We follow the mailbox down.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Whoa. It’s a post office for things that don’t have anywhere to go.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Dead letters. Every undelivered thing in the city ends up under it. Birthday cards. Thank-you notes. One pretzel.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That’s MY pretzel. I mean Rose’s. Rose’s pretzel. For Deedee.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Look at the big ledger. There’s a page for Second Avenue. There’s a blank rectangle where a name should be.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s still wet. Somebody erased him and left the space, like they were going to write somebody else in.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: There are four doors, one for each of us.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Four people who would never forget him. Behind each door there must be a memory of Tom that only one of us has.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: If we bring them back to this desk, maybe his name comes back too.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The desk in the middle has four little brass niches in the front. Four of us, four niches. And a chair that someone just stood up out of.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: There’s a thermos on it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s his. I’d know that thermos in the dark.

lines.speaker: Dead-Letter Office
lines.text: Four keepsakes glow in four brass niches. The bell sits on the counter. Rose reaches up, stands on her tiptoes, and rings it.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: Good evening. The Office is closed. May I help you? You look lost, which is the right way to look in here.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We’re here for a name. A man named Tom, on Second Avenue.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I erased him. His name was too loud for its line on the page, so I tidied it away. It is not personal. I tidy everything that does not fit.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He’s my brother.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I am sure he is lovely. He is also unclaimed. Everything here is. That is the best a thing can be, Mrs. Gregori: safe and unclaimed.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can’t erase somebody because he doesn’t fit your form.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: It is the only thing I am for. No one has ever handed me a letter to deliver. They only hand me returns.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: That’s the saddest job in the world.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: It is a very tidy job.

lines.text: Please step back from the desk. I am going to finish erasing the name.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. We can do this again. It’s a pottery rule: the first one always cracks.

lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. We can do this again. It’s a pottery rule: the first one always cracks.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Censor lowers his stamp. The black bar over his face slides to the side, a little at a time, and under it is only a small tired man with ink on his cuffs.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I have never been argued with by so many people at once. It was... full.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sorry I was late. I was written out of the schedule. I’ll sort it out with accounting.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: TATA!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: TATA!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello. Hello. Yes. Careful of the glasses. The glasses have been through a lot.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You absolute marshmallow. You were GONE. You ate nothing. You skipped lunch for a whole afternoon, and then a night.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I had a granola bar. It was written out too. I haven’t felt this hungry since the nineties.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara arrives at about a hundred miles an hour and climbs directly onto Tom. Nobody tries to stop her.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. I know. I missed you too. I was a small gold light and I missed you the whole time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He turns to the Censor, who is looking at the floor.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You have never delivered anything.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Rose.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Here. It’s a little bit squished. It’s for Deedee. It was held for pickup, but nobody picked it up, because she’s stone.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then here’s your first delivery route. Take this one pretzel up fifty-nine floors of one tower, and put it in a grandmother’s hands.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I do not... I have never left the Office.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The route is not far. The job is only to put a thing in someone’s hands. You are already very good at the part where you carry it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Censor takes the pretzel in both hands, carefully, as if it were made of glass. Then he lifts his stamp, looks at it, and brings it down on the napkin. It does not say RETURN TO SENDER. It says DELIVERED.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: It is a nicer word to hold than I expected.

lines.speaker: Dead-Letter Office
lines.text: In the big ledger, the clean white rectangle fills itself in, one slow letter at a time. T. O. M. The ink is the exact blue of a thermos cap.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. Home. Food. Then Mom and Dad. In that order.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: In that order.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Talking to the stone does nothing. I’ve checked. What wakes stone up is being warm for a long time, with people close by.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom’s rule: a house is warm when somebody is cooking in it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So we cook.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A lot. We cook a LOT.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: Tom! You’re BACK. I saw the light on at four a.m. and I thought, he’s home, and then I thought, no, that’s a different kind of light. I made a lasagna.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: I brought a rock. Lachlan picked it out. Isla ate a different rock. We’re keeping a close eye on it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you. All of you. I’ll put the rock on the mantel.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: I heard there was a situation. I brought lemon bars. And peppers. My nephew grows them. They’re very hot. A man called Boppy would know what to do.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy would eat one raw and say it was “fine” in a voice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The kitchen is a mess. Every pot is in use. The window is fogged. It smells like a Sunday.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The oven door handle came off. I fixed it. You could say I handled it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Please stop.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lasagna, eleven minutes. Lemon bars, six. I have a timer on everything. Nobody is allowed to be late for this.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I choreographed the pasta. It goes from the pot to the plate in a very specific arc.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m the taster. I’ve tasted nine times. It’s for quality.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The pasta does not go in an arc.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It goes in an arc if you believe in it, Tata.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looks at the table. Everyone he loves is crowded around it, and somebody has put a rock in the middle like a centerpiece. He doesn’t say anything for a second.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Pack it all up. Sal is outside with cab seven. Mom and Dad are still stone in that snow globe on floor fifty-nine, so we’re bringing dinner to them.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Cab seven! Everybody in. Bring the lasagna on your lap, it holds the heat. Fifty-nine floors, no stops, I’m not even charging.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I’m scared of that tower and I’m going anyway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The snow globe is still on its plinth. Inside it, very small, two stone figures hold each other up. The amber light is crawling on their hands. It is slower than before.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom. Dad. We brought dinner.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I brought a pretzel. It has been DELIVERED. It has a stamp.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Everybody sit. Around the plinth. Nobody leave. Plates on laps.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Steam from the lasagna drifts across the glass. The amber light turns the color of toast. A crack of warm yellow runs along the stone, then two, then nine.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s working. It’s working!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Oh. Oh, my back. My back is going to be talking about this for a week.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is that lasagna? Who made lasagna? Who’s been in my kitchen?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: DEEDEE! BOPPY!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh, my babies. Come here. All of you. Come here, to the moon and back and back and back.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Which one of you is eating the peppers raw?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Nobody. Yet.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Hand me one. For my knees.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Everyone is crowded onto one floor of a glass tower with plates in their laps, and for a minute, it is just a family having dinner, eight people and a dog.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom. Who is the man in the gold coat? The one who kept us on a shelf?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Vance. He’s still up there, at the top. He’s going to want more than a shelf.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then we finish eating first.
