lines.speaker: Stillness Core
lines.text: Eight lamps light round the frame of the lift in the middle of the Core, one for each of you. The brass doors slide apart, and a warm gold light comes out of the shaft.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He built a lock that opens for family. All eight of us, and a thermos. I resent how much I admire that.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That’s the Extra Place. Mom has set a place for everybody at every dinner for fifty years, plus one more.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: A lock that only opens when the whole family shows up? She could have told him how that works.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is it ready? Because I made a lot.

lines.speaker: Stillness Core
lines.text: THE EXTRA PLACE (the all-eight Family Finish) is ready. It costs 75% HEART.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: In the ceiling of the Vault, a round brass door has opened. It has a clock for a keyhole. It is ticking very slowly, like a heart that has been told to be quiet.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That’s the biggest clock I’ve ever seen. And I have a lot of clocks. They all run fast, for my stomach.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is that the man’s house? Somebody should tell him to leave a light on.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody stays together. All eight. Nobody goes through a door alone.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Nara goes first. She’s the best at doors.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Eight of us, a dog and a thermos. Seconds first, then the sky. Let’s go.

lines.speaker: Stillness Core
lines.text: The lift opens into a round chamber of brass and glass, behind the face of the sky clock. Every wall is a gear, and every gear is turning very slowly. Eight round doors stand sealed around a lift in the middle. Each keyhole is shaped like somebody.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I get a door too?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You get a door too.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s a very good lock. Whoever made it really cared about the mechanism.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Each door opens for one person’s best skill. Find the door shaped like you, and do the thing you’re best at.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: A column of gears the height of a tower. Around it, a brass serpent as long as a street is slowly uncoiling. Every scale is a clock face. Every clock says 4:59. At the top of the Engine, on a platform of glass, a man in a long coat stands with his back to you.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. You came back. You always come back. That is the thing I could never forgive you for.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I was written out of the schedule. I’m a very stubborn calendar entry.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Everything leaves. Time takes a little every day, and then one day all of it. So I built a place where it cannot. The Leviathan keeps every afternoon exactly as it was. Please do not hurt it. It is all I have.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You turned my grandparents into STATUES.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I kept them safe.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I was a statue for a week and my back didn’t get a single day off. I’d like to file a complaint.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Julian, honey. Have you eaten?

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: There are four things that will keep you out. Distance. Age. Exhaustion. Fear. Four things I could never get past. You will not, either.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Distance, age, exhaustion, fear. That’s just a regular Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. Four barriers. We have a plan for every one of them. Everybody ready?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is the snake going to be mean?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s going to be very, very tired. Be kind about it, and be fast.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: The Chronos-Leviathan lowers its head. Every clock on its body ticks at once.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. It’s a long fight, and we’re a long family. We can do this again.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. It’s a long fight, and we’re a long family. We can do this again.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: The Leviathan comes apart. It does not die. It comes apart like a watch being taken out of its case, one gear at a time, every one of them still ticking.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: Where its coil was, there is a room made of glass. A small living room. One lamp, one armchair. A man in a long coat is sitting in it with his hat in his hands. He is a good deal smaller than the shadow he threw.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: My daughter was nine. I was on a flight. I told her, one more flight next month. It was her birthday. I told my mother the same thing, about the hospital. I told my partner the same thing about everything.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: There was always one more flight next month. And then there was not. So I stopped the months. I did not know how to say goodbye. So I made sure that nobody could leave.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Julian.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Eternal Silence.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: Every sound in the Engine goes out. Every move you have turns to grey stone, and the stone falls and lies on the glass floor. He did not fight. He only went quiet, and asked everyone to.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He’s not attacking us. Look at his hands.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: They’re shaking.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is he cold?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No hitting. He has done enough to everybody else. Do the thing you’re each best at, for him. Everybody. In turn. I’ll be last.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The last one is always the hardest. That’s why I put the pepper first.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody up. He’s not going anywhere. That’s rather the point of him.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody up. He’s not going anywhere. That’s rather the point of him.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: Julian is still in the armchair. He has a cardigan on and a tennis ball in his lap, and a plate of rhubarb crisp that he has not eaten. The glass of the living room is cracked right down the middle, and every crack is letting the light in.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Clara would be thirty-one. She would say I deserved all of this.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Probably. And then she would sit down next to you anyway.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I could not make the minute stop hurting. So I stopped the minute. It did not stop hurting. It only stopped.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Honey. That’s all of it. That’s what living is. It hurts a little, every time, and you do it anyway.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: And the crisp is excellent.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I do not know how to start the clocks.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You don’t start them. You stop holding them.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: Julian lets go. A long breath goes out of him, the one that has been in him for twenty years. The Forever Engine lets go with him. One by one, every gear in the Moon begins to turn the right way, and far below, in two cities, every clock in the sky ticks forward, all together, to five o’clock.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: IT MOVED! The clock MOVED!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s five o’clock. It’s just five o’clock. It’s the best five o’clock I have ever seen.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: The towns in the Archive are open. The coins are going home. The snow globe is a town again. I am sorry. I do not know how to say how sorry.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re doing it right now. Come to dinner.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I do not have anything to bring.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Bring yourself and an appetite.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: And bring a chair. We’re short a chair.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom already set the place. She set it at every dinner for fifty years. There’s always one more seat.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Long Island is a town again. The fountain is running. The library door is open. Someone has already started a pie, which is how you know it’s real.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Look! Look who’s delivering!

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: Good afternoon. I have four parcels. This is the first delivery I have ever made. Please do not be too nice about it. I am a little emotional.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: My squishy! The Sparkling Diamond Gold Soup Dumpling squishy!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: My pink ribbon! It’s still tied in a bow!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: My stopwatch. It’s still running. It’s at nine hundred and eleven hours, and some seconds.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: My first cup. It’s full. It’s still warm. I don’t know how that’s possible and I’m not going to ask.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: Each one is stamped DELIVERED. It is, I have learned, my favorite word.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He hands me a fifth parcel. It is small and brown. It is addressed, in my own handwriting, to Tom, Second Avenue. It is a letter I never mailed.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I did not open it. That is not my department anymore. I only deliver.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Cab seven! Everybody in! I’m not charging. I’m not even driving. Look UP.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: High over the Square, a line of gold runs from the sky down to the fountain. There is a rail on it with a seam of bright gold, exactly where somebody mended it. A train glides in, quiet as a held breath. The sign on its front says LONG ISLAND on one side and LOS ANGELES on the other.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I made it from the Engine. It runs both coasts. It does not stop the clocks. It only makes the distance a little shorter. I thought, if I had built that first...

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You would have been home for the birthday.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I would have been home.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: A SKYWAY TRAIN?! I don’t know what to do with my hands! I’m a cab driver!

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: You’re the first passenger. Get in the train.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Three thousand miles. One ride. Mom, Dad, you can come to Tom’s any Tuesday you like.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Does it have a recliner?

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: It has four. I asked.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I’ve changed my mind about the man.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I am going to call my daughter. I do not know whether she will pick up. I am going to call anyway.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s a good seat to start in.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A week later. Jefferson Park, six in the evening. The street light has come on, and for once it is not worth mentioning.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, the train came again. It has a snack cart. It has a snack CART.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I rode both coasts in one day. I did a floor routine in the dining car. Nobody stopped me.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Boppy fell asleep in the recliner somewhere over Nebraska. He says it’s the best nap of his life. He says his back has never felt worse.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Both of those are true.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Justin is coming out on the next one. He booked his own ticket. He says he cleared the whole weekend.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ve been looking at the calendar for an hour to make sure it’s real.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: LAAAAA! The piano works!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Mom. Inside voice.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That WAS my inside voice.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's the big note from the end of act one! Keep going, I know the next part!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Now there are TWO of them.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The Rivituso Rule. No throwing at the teacher. It's still painted on the wall.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Seven o'clock exactly. On my watch too.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That's MY red pen! I dropped my clipboard at recess when the flash went off, and when I picked it up the pen was gone!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy, your pen is as tall as a door! And it's wearing glasses!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy, he's the mean judge! Like on our shows!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: There's always a mean judge. And he always cries in the finale.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: At recess there was a big flash, and now I'm big enough to grade everybody. I made the bells and the clocks wrong so that everybody would be late. Late is late. Points off.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: And YOU. With the binder. Tab three is crooked.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It is NOT crooked!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...It's a little crooked.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: And it has a gold star on its clip!

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: That's the only gold star in this school that isn't a sticker. I found it in the grass. I'm saving it for one perfect paper. There has never been one.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The mean judge cried in the finale. I called it.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori. When an answer is wrong, you write "good try" next to my X. I always thought that was silly. It isn't.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: One perfect paper. This is for you.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I got a gold star! Wait until Mom sees this. I'm her favorite this year, so my picture goes on the front of the Christmas tree.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It dropped its gold star on my clipboard. I'm keeping it. Wait until Mom sees this. I'm her favorite this year, so my picture goes on the front of the Christmas tree.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom calls me her favorite son every single time I walk in the door!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You're her ONLY son, Tom.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's a gold coin, Mom. It has a kickball on it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Rose has a dragonfly. I have a lemon. Boppy has a fish and TNB has a cowboy hat. And now you have a kickball.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Five coins and five orange blocks. Grace, put it on the list.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's already on the list.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you! That's been bothering me for ten whole minutes.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The sign-up sheet! It's a bit crumpled. But every name is spelled right.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Mom, can I keep it? I'll keep it inside Lamby.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It stays on my clipboard. Not inside Lamby.

lines.speaker: Mr. Delgado
lines.text: She said my son is KIND!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A parent is crying! Tab three! I know this one!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "Tissue first. Then a cookie."

lines.speaker: Mr. Delgado
lines.text: Thank you. That's a very good binder.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I KNOW!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Thirty parents, and the only one who cried was happy. Tom, that was better than a season finale.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And nobody flipped a table!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I had a tab ready for that.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Thirty conferences. One gold star. One very well-behaved pen.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The ball is STILL up there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's really hanging in there.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Six. I'm telling TNB.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He'll be so proud.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: On Monday morning I have to explain that to the whole school.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I have two burnt flashbulbs in my pocket, and nobody can explain those to me.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Those go to Mom. She called me four times about her rule. Nobody goes anywhere alone.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I put all five on one page. Mine has a chart.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Can I have a copy for tab four?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can have a copy. The chart stays with me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Can I keep the binder?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It's yours. I made it for you. Your name is on the spine.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: My name is on the SPINE!
